notes: IFRS throughout FY2007-FY2025 (IFRS as endorsed by the EU, also full IFRS); no change of accounting standard in the period, so a standard switch is not a factor. Fiscal year ends September 30; fiscalYear is the calendar year the fiscal year ends in.
revenue = the revenue line of the consolidated income statement (continuing operations), read from the latest document that republished the year (normally the five-year summary of a later report).

operatingIncome = 'Income from continuing operations before income taxes'. Siemens publishes no consolidated EBIT / operating-profit line (its segments report an 'operating profit', but that is not a group income-statement line).

netIncome = net income attributable to shareholders of Siemens AG; totalEquity = total equity attributable to shareholders of Siemens AG. The five-year summaries print only the totals including non-controlling interests (FY2025: total net income EUR 10,387m, total equity EUR 68,371m), so the attributable figures were read from the consolidated income statement and statement of financial position.

totalDebt = the 'Debt' line of the five-year summaries / 'Total debt' of the 20-F capital structure tables = short-term debt and current maturities of long-term debt plus long-term debt. Taken as published, not summed.
capex = 'Additions to intangible assets and property, plant and equipment' from the cash flow statement (in the older 20-Fs the same line), stored negative.

dilutedEPS is the diluted earnings per share for continuing and discontinued operations (the whole-group line: FY2025 EUR 12.11), matching the whole-group netIncome; Siemens also prints a continuing-operations EPS (FY2025 EUR 9.52) which is not used here.

totalEquity for FY2010-FY2013 is the attributable figure published in the capital-structure tables of the Form 20-F filings (FY2013: EUR 28,111m, confirmed again in the FY2014 annual report); no later document republishes attributable equity for those years, because the later five-year summaries carry only total equity including non-controlling interests. FY2010 and FY2011 attributable equity and cash are from the FY2011 Form 20-F, i.e. before IFRS 11 was applied (IFRS 11 left FY2013 attributable equity unchanged at 28,111).

sharesOutstanding = shares outstanding at September 30 for FY2007-FY2013 (disclosed in Item 3 of the 20-F filings). From FY2014 the annual reports publish no period-end count, so the basic weighted average number of shares outstanding from the earnings-per-share note is used (FY2025: 785,093 thousand). The two definitions differ by less than 1%.
employees = headcount at September 30 on a continuing-operations basis as printed in the five-year summaries; null for FY2007-FY2009 (see gaps).

Restatement chain, latest figure used each time: IFRS 11 (adopted FY2014) removed proportionate consolidation of joint ventures and cut FY2010-FY2013 revenue by about 4% (FY2010 67,862 -> 65,067; FY2011 72,526 -> 69,607; FY2012 77,395 -> 74,734 -> 74,087; FY2013 75,882 -> 73,445 -> 72,782) while total net income was unchanged. IFRS 15 from FY2018 restated FY2017 (revenue 83,049 -> 82,863, total assets 133,804 -> 136,111, diluted EPS 7.29 -> 7.19, net income attributable 6,046 -> 5,961, employees 372 -> 377). IFRS 9 from the Sep 30, 2018 balance sheet; IFRS 17 in the Sep 30, 2023 balance sheet.

Scope breaks to be aware of: Siemens Energy and Siemens Gamesa were classified as discontinued operations in FY2020, Flender in FY2021 and Innomotics in FY2024. From FY2018 the reported revenue, operating cash flow, capex and employees are continuing operations only (FY2018 revenue 83,044 -> 55,538; FY2019 86,849 -> 56,797; FY2022 71,977 -> 69,519; FY2023 77,769 -> 74,882), while netIncome is the whole-group figure attributable to shareholders and therefore still contains the discontinued businesses. FY2017 revenue (82,863) is on the pre-FY2020 basis because Siemens did not restate periods before FY2018.

FY2007-FY2009 come from the Form 20-F filings (Siemens' last 20-F is fiscal 2013). Nothing republished them after IFRS 11, so their revenue is on the older basis (FY2009: 70,053 originally, 68,726 in the 2013 filing), whereas FY2010-FY2011 revenue are the IFRS 11 values from the FY2014 annual report. Net income attributable for FY2007-FY2009 is the figure published before those reclassifications (FY2007 3,806, FY2008 5,725, FY2009 2,292).

20-F source references point to the EDGAR HTML filings: Item/section plus the F-page numbers of the audited statements in Item 18, because no paginated PDF of those filings was used. Where a year needed two documents, the second document's URL is given in the source.document text.

Five-year-summary links: Siemens stores each year's 'Five-Year Summary' PDF under a content hash that changes when the file is re-published, so the three summary links (fiscal 2017, 2018 and 2019 editions) were refreshed from the hashes that the IR annual-reports page (irUrl) currently publishes and the cited columns re-read; every URL in this file was re-opened and returned a PDF/HTML document.

Yahoo cross-check (snapshot-2026-10-26, USD at the fiscal-year average rate): FY2025 revenue 78,914 x 1.1066 = 87,320 vs 87,320; FY2024 75,930 x 1.0872 = 82,550 vs 82,548; FY2025 net income 9,620 x 1.1066 = 10,645 vs 10,645; FY2024 8,301 x 1.0872 = 9,025 vs 9,025; FY2023 and FY2022 net income also match at the average rates (8,509 and 4,020). The only gap above 3% is FY2022 revenue: Yahoo carries USD 77,716, which corresponds to the pre-Innomotics figure of EUR 71,977m, while this file uses the restated EUR 69,519m (about 3.4% lower).
